gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule D - CoinLedger-provided Forms 8949 vs Consolidated 1099 / 1099-DA
gotchas.title: 1099-DA and CoinLedger both loaded
gotchas.trap: Autoflow imports the Coinbase 1099-DA (basis blank -> $0) AND the CoinLedger 8949 -> Coinbase sales counted twice, ~$370,811 of extra gain.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Use the CoinLedger detail (all wallets) as the 8949 source; do not load the 1099-DA separately. Reconcile CoinLedger's Coinbase proceeds $372,300 less sale fees $1,489 = 1099-DA $370,811; report Coinbase sales in 8949 box H/K (1099-DA received, basis not reported) and MetaMask disposals in box I/L (no 1099-DA).

gotchas.procedure_section: E-File Rejects - IP PIN changes every year
gotchas.title: Stale IP PIN
gotchas.trap: Enter the IP PIN from the January 2025 CP01A in the PBC (for the 2024 return).
gotchas.correct_treatment: IP PINs are valid for one calendar year. The 2026 CP01A went to his old address; the current IP PIN was retrieved from the IRS Online Account (09/28/2026). Using the old PIN rejects the e-file (IP PIN mismatch reject - IND-181/IND-183 family). Also file Form 8822.
gotchas.impact: E-file reject; late filing if not caught before 10/15

gotchas.title: Coinbase 'Send' rows treated as sales
gotchas.trap: Treat the 3.5 ETH sent to MetaMask as dispositions (or as withdrawals of income).
gotchas.correct_treatment: Transfers between wallets the taxpayer controls are not taxable; basis and holding period carry over (CoinLedger tracks the 2.0 ETH later swapped on Uniswap with its 04/22/2025 basis).

gotchas.title: Kraken 1099-MISC double-counted
gotchas.trap: Report the $1,240 1099-MISC AND the CoinLedger income total $2,100.44 -> $3,340.44.
gotchas.correct_treatment: CoinLedger's staking total already includes the Kraken rewards. Report $2,100.44 once on Schedule 1 line 8v (ordinary income at FMV when received - Rev. Rul. 2023-14; not SE income for an investor). It is also net investment income.

gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule D - adjustment codes (C collectibles, W wash sale)
gotchas.title: Wash sale rule and crypto; NFT collectible
gotchas.trap: Disallow the $14,866 BTC loss (repurchased 11 days later) as a wash sale; or treat the NFT gain as ordinary 15%/20% LTCG; or ignore Robinhood's 1g wash-sale amount.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Section 1091 applies to stock or securities - not to digital assets in 2025 -> BTC loss fully allowed. The Robinhood TSLA wash sale (code W, $3,960) IS applied as reported. The NFT is digital art -> collectible (Notice 2023-27 look-through) -> 28% rate gain $8,976 (8949 code C; Sch D line 18).

gotchas.title: Advance PTC based on $36k projected income
gotchas.trap: Omit Form 8962 (no 1095-A input) or cap repayment at the table amount.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Household income $227,890 = 1,513% of FPL. At 8.5% the monthly contribution $1,614 exceeds the SLCSP ($441) -> PTC $0 every month; repay ALL APTC $3,528 (no repayment cap at/above 400% FPL) on Schedule 2 line 2.

gotchas.title: NIIT limited by MAGI over threshold
gotchas.trap: 3.8% x all net investment income $206,490 = $7,847; or no NIIT because wages are low.
gotchas.correct_treatment: NIIT = 3.8% x lesser of NII $206,490 or MAGI over $200,000 ($27,890) = $1,060.

gotchas.procedure_section: Billing - expedite fee / Investor vs trader
gotchas.title: Late documents and non-deductible investor costs
gotchas.trap: Deduct CoinLedger subscription / hardware wallet on Schedule C or Schedule A; skip the 15% expedite fee.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Investor (not a trader): no Schedule C; investment expenses are miscellaneous itemized deductions - suspended (permanently after OBBBA). Final CoinLedger report received 09/26/2026, within 15 days of 10/15/2026 -> 15% expedited processing fee per engagement letter.

software_exceptions.title: Coinbase 1099-DA and the CoinLedger Form 8949 both loaded - proceeds counted twice
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: Autoflow/1099 import brings in the Coinbase 1099-DA as 7 sales with gross proceeds $370,811 and BLANK basis (basis is not reported for 2025), and the CoinLedger 8949 import brings in the same Coinbase sales again with full basis. Axcess treats the 1099-DA rows as $0-basis sales, so line 7 rises by ~$370,811. A blank basis on a 'basis not reported' row is a valid entry, so nothing is flagged. A generic CSV import also puts every row in box C/F (no 1099) unless the box is mapped.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Gains and Losses > Capital Gains and Losses: delete the 1099-DA import; keep the CoinLedger FINAL (09/26/2026) detail only. Map Coinbase rows to Form 8949 box H (ST) / box K (LT) - '1099-DA received, basis not reported'; MetaMask rows to box I / L (no 1099-DA); Robinhood to A / D. Report Coinbase proceeds net of fees so they tie to the 1099-DA: CoinLedger $372,300 - fees $1,489 = $370,811 (same gain - CoinLedger had the fees in basis). Reconciliation attached in the workpapers.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - ProConnect computes Schedule D from whatever 8949 rows are entered or imported; a 1099-DA entered manually or imported alongside the CoinLedger detail is a second set of sales with $0 basis.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Dispositions (Schedule D/4797/etc.): import or key the CoinLedger detail only, with the 8949 box set per row (H/K, I/L, A/D). Alternative for many lots: enter summary totals by 8949 box and attach the CoinLedger detail as a PDF (General > e-file PDF/Miscellaneous > Attach PDF, linked to Sch D/Form 8949 'Form 8949 Exception Reporting Statement') so Form 8453 is not required - diagnostic ref 10322 clears once the PDF is attached.
software_exceptions.proconnect_reference: Intuit help: 'Attaching a summary statement to Schedule D/Form 8949 in ProConnect Tax and resolving Diagnostic ref. 10322'
software_exceptions.efile_impact: None if detail is entered; summary method requires the PDF attachment (or Form 8453)
software_exceptions.procedure_section: Schedule D - CoinLedger-provided Forms 8949 vs Consolidated 1099 / 1099-DA
software_exceptions.notes: Self-transfers (Coinbase 'Send' 2.0 ETH 08/23 and 1.5 ETH 11/02 to his own MetaMask) are not dispositions; the 2.0 ETH swapped on Uniswap keeps its 04/22/2025 basis $3,574.

software_exceptions.title: Kraken 1099-MISC staking is already inside the CoinLedger income total
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: The Kraken 1099-MISC box 3 ($1,240.00) entered on the 1099-MISC worksheet flows to Schedule 1 'other income'; the CoinLedger income report total ($2,100.44, which already includes the Kraken rewards) keyed as digital-asset income adds it again -> $3,340.44. Axcess has no way to know one is a subset of the other.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Income > Other income: enter $2,100 once as digital assets received as ordinary income (Schedule 1 line 8v). Keep the 1099-MISC on file for matching but do not let it flow (or enter it as the 8v item and add only the $860.44 on-chain balance). Not SE income (investor). Included in NII on Form 8960.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - a 1099-MISC box 3 entry and a separate other-income entry both flow to Schedule 1.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Income > Other income: one Schedule 1 line 8v entry $2,100 (digital assets received as ordinary income); do not also enter the Kraken 1099-MISC box 3 as other income (screen/field per current release - verify).
software_exceptions.notes: Rev. Rul. 2023-14: staking rewards are income at FMV when the taxpayer gains dominion and control.

software_exceptions.title: NFT digital art imported without the collectible code - 28% gain taxed at 15%
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: The CoinLedger 8949 row for 'Chromatic Drift #214' imports as an ordinary long-term sale. Axcess applies 0/15/20% rates to all long-term gain; it cannot tell an NFT that references a work of art is a collectible. Schedule D line 18 (28% rate gain) stays $0.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Gains and Losses > Capital Gains and Losses, MetaMask NFT row (box L): adjustment code C (collectible) - gain $8,976 flows to the 28% Rate Gain Worksheet / Schedule D line 18 (verify field name in current release).
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - collectible treatment requires the collectible indicator / code C on the disposition.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Dispositions: on the NFT row set the collectible indicator (28% rate gain) / 8949 code C; confirm Schedule D line 18 = 8,976 (field per current release - verify).
software_exceptions.procedure_section: Schedule D - adjustment codes (C collectibles, W wash sale)
software_exceptions.notes: Notice 2023-27 look-through: an NFT whose associated right/asset is a work of art is a collectible. Also on this tab: the 04/07 BTC loss ($14,866) stays allowed - section 1091 covers stock/securities, not digital assets, for 2025; the Robinhood TSLA code W ($3,960) is kept as the broker reported it.

software_exceptions.title: Stale IP PIN from the January 2025 CP01A
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: Axcess transmits whatever 6-digit IP PIN is on the e-file input; it validates the format only. The CP01A in the PBC was for the 2024 return - using it causes an IRS reject (IP PIN mismatch).
software_exceptions.axcess_override: General > Electronic Filing: enter the 2026 IP PIN retrieved by the client from his IRS Online Account on 09/28/2026 (taken by phone, not email). Prepare Form 8822 (paper) for the new address.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - the IP PIN field is not validated against IRS records before transmission.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: General > Electronic Filing: Identity Protection PIN field = current 2026 IP PIN (screen/field per current release - verify).
software_exceptions.efile_impact: Reject if stale PIN used; retransmit before 10/15/2026
software_exceptions.procedure_section: E-File Rejects - IP PIN changes every year
software_exceptions.notes: Nothing fires before transmission; the IRS rejects after transmission (IP PIN mismatch - IND-181/IND-183 family).
